as_of_rule: historical prices capped at derived expected pricing date; no look-ahead
limitations: 95 rows had recognizable index baskets and recoverable expected pricing dates; remaining rows are blocked rather than guessed
barriers/coupon schedules are not fully semantic-validated for every row
derived expected dates are not verified issuance dates

review.interpretation: The replay shows critical data pipeline failures: 877 rows blocked due to unrecoverable pricing dates and 1,029 due to unmapped underlyings, indicating systemic data ingestion issues rather than isolated edge cases. While the 86 completed predictions show technically correct simulation execution (mean p_loss=0.0, avg_payoff=1.2619), the high block rates invalidate the statistical representativeness of these results. The absence of verification outcomes (Verified outcomes=0) and null performance metrics (Brier/log-loss/ECE/accuracy) further confirm that no meaningful validation was possible.
objections: Critical data pipeline failures (877 + 1,029 blocked rows) invalidate the sample size and representativeness
No verification outcomes (Verified outcomes=0) means no ground truth comparison was performed
Performance metrics are null (Brier/log-loss/ECE/accuracy=null), indicating no proper evaluation
Production flags are false, suggesting the system is not ready for deployment
The 8 blocked rows for missing market history are acceptable, but the other block rates are not
acceptance_tests: Verify that all 2,000 rows can be processed without blocking (target: 0 blocked rows)
Confirm that pricing dates and underlyings are properly mapped for all securities
Establish a minimum threshold for completed predictions (e.g., >95% of total rows)
Implement verification mechanisms to ensure Verified outcomes > 0
Define and compute performance metrics (Brier score, log-loss, ECE, accuracy) on verified outcomes
review.next_experiment: Fix data pipeline issues to eliminate blocking, then rerun the replay with the same 2,000 rows to verify that all rows are processed and metrics can be computed. Focus on mapping underlyings and recovering pricing dates before proceeding with further analysis.
